reason: The storm may cut solar power, so putting the station on its charged reserve addresses the current goal.
expectation: I expect the shutdown controls to switch the station to reserve power, perhaps also stopping industrial loads; the exact sequence is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The outdoor water line will lose heat, so its shutdown may also be needed, but the reserve seems like a useful first step.
Moving the heat store into the nook could protect the garden, but the station's power transition is the immediate goal.

effect: The reserve now powers essential loads, but the garden's normal circulation is off, so its survival equipment will need the nook's outlets.
reaction: The dimmed lights and stopped circulation make the storm's consequences feel immediate.
reason: The outdoor line will lose heat, so I want to address it at the shutdown controls before moving the garden.
expectation: I expect the line to be isolated or otherwise protected against freezing, though I don't know the exact procedure.

alternatives.reason: The heat store could help protect the crops, but the exposed water line also needs attention.

effect: The outdoor line is drained and isolated, with its pump and thaw checks on essential power. The remaining goal is to move both troughs and the heat store into the nook.
reaction: Draining the actual line makes the freeze protection clear; keeping thaw checks powered is a useful detail.
reason: The heat store can provide warmth in the sheltered nook, so I’ll move it in before the troughs.
expectation: I expect the charged tank to be placed in the nook, ready to release heat slowly around the beds.

alternatives.reason: The lettuce also needs shelter, but I want to put the heat source in place first.

effect: The heat store is in the nook, where it will help during the first cold hours while reserve power supplies longer-term heating.
reaction: The distinction between stored warmth and longer-term heating makes the setup clearer.
reason: Both troughs need shelter, so I’ll move the lettuce in next.
expectation: I expect the lettuce trough to be placed inside the warmed nook; it may still need its survival equipment connected.

alternatives.reason: The potato trough also needs shelter, and I have no clear reason to prioritize either bed.

effect: The lettuce is sheltered with its own reservoir, and its common-return couplings are capped. The potato trough still needs to move into the nook.
reaction: Carrying the bed level and protecting its leaves makes the move feel practical.
reason: Moving the potato trough is the only remaining combination and completes the stated move into the nook.
expectation: I expect the potato trough to be placed in the sheltered nook alongside the lettuce and heat store.

effect: The potato trough is sheltered alongside the lettuce and heat store, completing the chapter’s goals.
reaction: Keeping the potato bed’s cover, support and reservoir together makes the move feel concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Draining and isolating the outdoor line was most worthwhile: it showed a practical way to protect it when its heat is lost, while keeping thaw checks powered.

leastWorthwhile.text: Moving the two troughs felt somewhat repetitive, although each passage gave useful details about handling the beds.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the warm tank would help only through the first cold hours, with reserve power needed for longer-term heating.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; each addressed the storm preparations, though I had no clear reason to move lettuce before potatoes.

continue.text: Yes. I’m curious how the storm and early return will affect the specimens and what the lab will learn from them.
